classification.difficultyReason: Combine the tangent-radius right angle, triangle angle sum and the centre-to-circumference angle relationship.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: Circle with centre O, external point P, tangent PT and radius OT. OP crosses the circumference at an unlabelled point. Two chords from an unlabelled left circumference point meet T and that intersection. The angle between those chords is w; angle OPT is 40 degrees.
spec.mathematics: PT is tangent at T. OT is a radius. The angle at O between OP and OT is 50 degrees; the circumference angle w stands on the same arc and is half that angle. Construction coordinates enforce tangency and the given angle without adding numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 40-degree angle and unknown w are visible; the supplied 25-degree answer is omitted.

answer.worked:
$\angle OTP=90^\circ$ because a tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
$$\begin{align*}\angle TOP+90^\circ+40^\circ&=180^\circ\\\angle TOP&=50^\circ\\w&=\frac{50^\circ}{2}\\w&=25^\circ\end{align*}$$
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
